summary: Write a first playbook in VS Code next to site.yml: a single play on localhost running ansible.builtin.ping. ansible-lint runs in the background and reports in the Problems tab; files must end with a blank line, have no trailing spaces, and every play needs a name.
questions: How do I write my first Ansible playbook in VS Code?
What lint rules does ansible-lint enforce on a new playbook?
Where does ansible-lint show errors in VS Code?

answer_card.title: Minimal first playbook
answer_card.answer_md:
```yaml
---
- name: My first play
  hosts: localhost
  tasks:
    - name: Ping my hosts
      ansible.builtin.ping:

```
Rules ansible-lint checks: end the file with a blank line, no trailing spaces, and give every play (and task) a `name`. Errors appear in the *Problems* tab.
